topics.title: Coordinates of a point: abscissa and ordinate

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the coordinates of a point to its distances from the y-axis and the x-axis.
Recognise that points on the x-axis have the form (x, 0) and points on the y-axis have the form (0, y).
Use the distance formula to find the distance between two points with given coordinates.
Find the distance of a point (x, y) from the origin as the square root of x squared plus y squared.
Decide whether three points are collinear by comparing the distances between them.
Classify a triangle or quadrilateral from the lengths of its sides and diagonals.
Find a point, or a relation between x and y, for a point equidistant from two given points.
Find the coordinates of the point dividing a line segment internally in a given ratio m1 : m2.
Write the coordinates of a point dividing a segment in the ratio k : 1.
Find the ratio in which a given point divides the segment joining two points.
Find the ratio in which a coordinate axis divides a segment and the point of intersection.
Find the mid-point of a segment and points dividing it into equal parts.
Use the mid-point formula with diameters of circles and diagonals of parallelograms.
